text: Heart Health Mini Guide (Test PDF) Overview Hypertension (high blood pressure) is a major risk factor for heart disease and stroke. In 2023, the World Health Organization (WHO) estimated that hypertension affects 1.28 billion adults worldwide. Key Conditions - Hypertension is defined as systolic 140 mmHg or diastolic 90 mmHg (clinic measurement). - Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (ASCVD) includes coronary artery disease and stroke. Treatments (examples) - Lisinopril (an ACE inhibitor) treats hypertension and helps reduce cardiovascular risk. - Atorvastatin (a statin) lowers LDL cholesterol, reducing ASCVD events. Guidelines & Organizations - The American Heart Association (AHA) recommends lifestyle changes (salt reduction, exercise 150 minutes/week) for adults with elevated BP. - The WHO reports global prevalence and publishes policy guidance for population-level BP control. Risk & Monitoring - Smoking increases the risk of heart disease and stroke. - Home BP monitors should be validated devices and used after 5 minutes of rest. Simple Facts (for relations) - Lisinopril treats Hypertension - Atorvastatin lowers LDL cholesterol - AHA recommends Lifestyle changes - WHO reports Hypertension prevalence - Smoking increases risk of Heart disease References - WHO. Hypertension fact sheet, 2023. - AHA. 2022/2023 guidance on BP management.
